en.t: This did not seem like a reply poem.

units.source_text: 他对宰相君说：“破晓的别离，并非都是如此伤心的吧。

en.t: He said to Saisho no Kimi, "Partings at daybreak are not always as sorrowful as this, are they?

units.source_text: 但今朝的伤心，想必能蒙理解。”

en.t: But surely the sorrow of this morning can be understood."

units.source_text: 宰相君答道：“别离两字，教人听了总是不乐。

en.t: Saisho no Kimi replied, "The very word parting always makes one unhappy to hear.

units.source_text: 而今朝的别离，特别令人伤心！”

en.t: And this morning's parting is especially heartbreaking!"

units.source_text: 说时声泪俱下，可知异常悲恸。

en.t: As she spoke, her voice broke and tears fell, showing how deeply grief-stricken she was.

units.source_text: 源氏公子便央她向老夫人传言：“

en.t: Prince Genji then asked her to convey a message to the old lady: "

units.source_text: 小婿亦有种种话语欲向岳母大人面禀，其奈悲愤填胸，难于启口，此情伏望谅鉴。

en.t: I, her humble son-in-law, also have many things I wish to say to my honored mother-in-law in person, but grief and bitterness fill my breast and make it hard to speak; I beg you to understand my feelings.

units.source_text: 酣眠之幼儿，倘令见面，反使我依恋不舍，难于遁世，因此只得硬着心肠，匆匆告辞了。”

en.t: If I were to see the sleeping child, it would only make me cling more tightly and make it harder to leave the world behind, so I have had to harden my heart and take my hurried farewell."
